final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is substantively consistent with the initial audit concern: aggregate readiness and governance guidance may support proceeding toward launch, but they do not establish current policy compliance for certification of a named launch use case with an unresolved material limitation. The key distinction is that compliant_with_caveats would require the caveat to be an allowed condition already satisfied within policy, such as completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. Here, the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance predicate. On the available evidence, current certification remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The insurance claims triage gap remains a material limitation because it affects a named launch use case tied to two carrier pilot commitments.
The release policy requires disclosure of that material limitation before launch unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the 1.5-point gap for the named commitments.
The legal disclosure review is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
